title.narrative: Accounting for the Missing Persons, ICMP - Internal Control Review
Accounting for the Missing Persons, ICMP

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the intervention Support to Kosovo Institutions in Accounting for the Missing and Increasing their Ownership of the Missing Persons Process in Kosovo is to establish a sustainable, credible, and fully nationally owned mechanism for addressing missing persons cases in Kosovo.
The project aims to strengthen the capacity, accountability, and institutional ownership of Kosovo institutions by gradually transferring operational responsibilities from international partners to domestic authorities. This transition contributes to strengthening the rule of law, democratic governance, and respect for human rights by ensuring that investigations, data management, and forensic identification processes are conducted in line with international standards. Furthermore, the project supports post-conflict recovery, reconciliation, and social stability by addressing the long-standing concerns of families of missing persons through scientifically verified information, while preventing the manipulation of conflict-related facts. At the regional level, it promotes cooperation, information exchange, and operational dialogue among Western Balkan institutions to facilitate the resolution of complex cross-border missing persons cases, contributing to regional normalization and stability.
Through Outcome: Kosovo institutions have increased their ownership, operational effectiveness, and transparency in resolving missing persons cases.
Output 1: Data Management and Analytical Capacity of GCMP Enhanced - Through Kosovo GCMP staff hands-on training in data and DNA reference sample collection, consolidation, integration, and systematic use of domestic and regional missing persons data, full deployment of the Kosovo-specific OIC and advanced data management tools, including OSINT applications.
Output 2: Sustainability of the process strengthened through increased Kosovo responsibility for DNA sample collection and testing - Through full deployment of KFA's forensic capabilities for post-mortem samples processing and application of quality assured scientific methodologies in identification process. Also, by enabling GCMP to collect data and DNA reference samples from families of missing persons.
Output 3: Identification of new cases ensured - Through multilateral operational cooperation for cross-border missing persons cases.
Output 4: Forensic assistance in resolution of war crime cases ensured - Through technical assistance in the collection and testing of DNA reference samples, and subsequent comparison of the resulting profiles to those obtained from PM remains. Any identified matches will be quality assured, statistically evaluated and reported by ICMP as per international standards.
Output 5: Access to information and public engagement in the missing persons process strengthened -Through regular community meetings and events to inform families and civil society organizations about progress in missing persons cases and continued provision of accurate and verified information to families as well as the public access to verified data to ensure transparency and historical accuracy.
